A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robotic imitation-learning study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original real-robot experiments on four manipulation tasks, including data-scaling results, model comparisons and success rates.

after.justification: V2 retains the original real-robot experiments and their outcomes in Figures 2–7, Tables 1–2 and the supplementary results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Diffusion Policy, DINOv2 visual encoder, temporal ensemble and data-collection strategy. Section 3 and Appendix C contain no procedural or architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Pour Water, Mouse Arrangement, Fold Towels and Unplug Charger. The object, environment and joint generalization scenarios, including the training and testing objects shown in Appendix A, are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same learning-from-scratch, frozen DINOv2, LoRA, visual-encoder-size and U-Net-size comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training subsets, demonstration counts, scoring criteria and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 4.1 and Appendix E retain the evaluations using eight unseen objects or environments and five trials each; the added uncertainty displays do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The multiple-objects-per-environment analysis, demonstration-saturation experiments and model ablations are retained. Appendices E and G preserve the same metric comparisons, MSE scaling analysis and controls for total demonstration count.

E5.justification: V2 adds shaded uncertainty bands to Figures 2–4 and 7; Section 4.1 explicitly identifies Figure 2's bands as 95% confidence intervals. Figure 5 now identifies its correlation coefficient as Pearson's r. Existing trial counts and Table 1 standard deviations remain unchanged, with no additional runs or interval-construction procedure documented.

E6.justification: The plotted means, fitted power-law coefficients, tabulated scores and qualitative findings are unchanged. Tables 1 and 12 retain success rates of 85.0%, 92.5%, 87.5% and 90.0% for the four tasks, respectively; Appendix G's raw-score tables are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The data-scaling formulation, optimality-gap definition, power-law equation and logarithmic transformation remain the same. The qualification concerning irreducible error and fitting only six data points is retained; no proof or mathematical argument is added.

C1.justification: The claims about approximate power laws, the importance of diversity and efficient collection yielding roughly 90% success remain unchanged. Adding 'within the same category' to the introductory question restates the scope already explicit in v1's abstract and Section 3.

C2.justification: The interpretations of diversity, demonstration saturation and model scaling are unchanged. Section 7 and the appendices retain the same limitations concerning single-task learning, four-task coverage, imitation learning, UMI data quality and evaluation comparability.

D1.justification: The data-collection instructions, training hyperparameters, computational resources, evaluation workflow and deployment hardware in Appendices B–F are unchanged. Code, data and model release statements and access links are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B.1 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The ACT citation receives only a punctuation correction.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording edits concerning object-category scope, confidence intervals and Pearson's r, corrects citation punctuation, updates funding acknowledgments and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header. Section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 and 7 are redrawn with translucent uncertainty bands and adjusted vertical ranges. Figure 5's caption is clarified, and some text shifts between pages. The figure/table inventory and appendix displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Adding uncertainty bands to the principal scaling plots makes the existing empirical evidence easier to assess, while identifying Pearson's r improves reporting precision. The gain is limited because v2 does not explain the confidence-interval calculation or sampling unit; the experiments, point estimates and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
